correctness.rationale: Independently integrated the polynomial powers using ∫z^i conjugate(z)^j dμ=δ_ij/(i+1). After sign choice and rotation the moments are as given; the phase dependence is exactly ab²C cos(ψ), forcing alignment when all degrees occur. At fixed q=C/a and nonzero a, the normalized linear-degree energy fraction makes the phase-aligned quotient quadratic with strictly positive initial and strictly negative final slopes. Its sole maximizer reproduces the claimed s(q) and rational envelope. The derivative factors as stated and changes sign once by Descartes' rule and the endpoint signs. Direct optimization on each coordinate face gives 7/3, 63/23 and 297/86, all below the unique interior optimum. In the (1,2) formula at lines 75–81 the printed fraction t is actually the degree-one fraction, contrary to the preceding 'second' convention; replacing t by 1−t puts the maximizing degree-two fraction at 25/43 rather than 18/43. This notational swap does not change the bound or any equality case in the Finding. All claimed constants and the strict gap are reproduced.
residual_risks: The check applies to real-valued polynomials and probability area, not to complex-valued harmonic polynomials, boundary mass or higher degree.
